Tianze's Otari Extras.description:
Introduction

Thank you for trying this module. Tianze's Otari Extras is a collection of maps and content set in the town of Otari, which is the setting for Pathfinder scenarios including Menace Under Otari (the Beginner Box adventure), Abomination Vaults Adventure Path and Troubles in Otari. 

Maps were created with DungeonDraft using assets from Forgotten Adventures.

Portraits and vignettes were created using Bing Image Creator.
Tianze's Otari Extras.caption: Tianze's Otari Extras is a collection of maps and content for the Otari area. It includes Crook's Nook and the Underbridge, Crow's Casks, Otari Market, the ruins of the Thirsty Alpaca and the Fish Camp Base.

Shop Journals.name: Shop Journals
Shop Journals.text:
NOTE: As of the release of v13, Monk's Enhanced Journals is indefinitely broken. He stated on his github that he does not know when he will have it fixed.

I am leaving these jouranls in this module for now, but be advised that the shop journals may not work properly. I have not tested them.

I have provided a set of merchant journals by user request. They require the Monk's Enhanced Journal module in order to function. It is in a separate optional compendium called "Tianze's Otari Shops."

Before importing it, keep in mind that it will require some setup.

  • The journals will be redundant since you will already have merchant tokens on many of the scenes. Here's what I recommend:

    • In the Actor folder, set "All Players" permission for each merchant actor to "none"

    • Replace the merchants in each scene. This way, they are visible but players are not able to interact with them.

    • Drag journal for the merchant out in front of each merchant actor. I have already set the "All Player" permission to "Observer" so your players will be able to interact with them.

I generated the contents of the journal shop inventories with rolltables that I crafted for each shop. They probably will not match the shop inventories of the merchant actors.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
Tianze's Otari Extras is a collection of maps and content set in the town of Otari, which is the setting for Pathfinder scenarios including Menace Under Otari (the Beginner Box adventure), Abomination Vaults Adventure Path and Troubles in Otari. 

I decided to create this module as an introductory free work for my adventurers and maps. I created the original version of these maps while running the adventure, and once I started improving the maps using Forgotten Adventures assets, I decided to try my hand at module-making.

Maps were created with DungeonDraft using assets from Forgotten Adventures.

Portraits and vignettes were created using Bing Image Creator and then refined and tokenized.

Macros were pulled together using using examples I found on either the Foundry's Reddit Pages, in the Macro Polo chat in Foundry's discord, or in the Abomination Vaults Adventure Path.

Update 3.1 - General Cleanup

I cleaned up some of the merchant actors that were configured as Item Piles, and which may have resulted in zero pricing.

Added a roletable for Weapons and Armor.

Repopulated several of the merchant actor inventories.

Removed some actors that no longer had token art, and that should have been removed last time.

What's Included

  • Crow's Casks

    • Map with tokens

    • Location Journal Pages

    • Encounter - Rowdy Gamblers

  • Crook's Nook

    • Bridge Map

    • Tavern Map with tokens

    • Upper Story Map with token

    • Location Journal Pages

    • An Invitation to the Osprey Club, a short adventure for a rogue character.

  • Otari Market

    • Map with tokens

    • Location Journal Pages

    • Encounter - Rival Gang

  • Into the Ruins, a short adventure based on an adventure hook from Abomination Vaults.

    • Ruin Map with tokens

    • Warren Map with tokens

    • Location Journal Pages

    • Actors and Items

  • Fish Camp

    • Fish camp map

    • Location journal pages

    • Encounter - Home Invasion, with tokens

  • Tavern Items

    • A menu of consumable items used to stock service merchants including inns, market vendors, and stables.

  • Merchant Actors with fully stocked inventory

    • 7 Merchant Actors based on Otari locations

    • 7 Original Merchants for the Otari Market

  • Convenience Macros

    • Many of the maps have tiny macros that will either toggle the visibility of tiles, or turn lights on and off at the same time. You can find these macros either in the relevant journal pages, or in the Macros folder. Look for the Otari Extras folder.

Encounter Assumptions

The encounters assume the party is around level 2 and have adventured around Otari. Perhaps they have completed one of the following:

  • Pathfinder Beginner Box

  • The starting scenarios in Troubles in Otari

  • The first level of Abomination Vaults

They should have already started to develop a positive reputation around town, and many of the merchants should at least know who they are.

Encounters and Map Philosophy

After making many maps that really served no purpose except for eye candy, maps such as inns and shops for which I never had enough miniatures or tokens to populate, I came up with the following rule:

Every map deserves an encounter.

Think of it as your creator's blessing for your map. After all, once you have a battle or other plot-moving encounter, the map setting is still available for its original purpose, whether it is an inn to stay at, a market to shop in, or a ruin to rebuild as a home base.

But to justify the existence of the map, I like to use it in some encounter that will move along the plot of the story I am trying to tell — whether it involves combat or not.

With that in mind, every map in this module has at least one encounter, which should fit into any Otari-based game.

Tavern Items

Players like things to buy, and eye candy to look at. These items give them something that will actually go into their inventory, and which they can then use by clicking that Consume button. Think of it as a virtual mug of ale, a virtual bath, or a virtual night in the room of an inn. These have been a big hit in my own games.

All tavern items use icons from the Foundry Core icons, and should persist in your game world.

The drink agnar is a hot stimulating beverage, similar to coffee or tea, and is my own invention.

Merchant Actors

The merchant actors were inspired by an excellent little content mod called PF2e a shopping experience. However, I created my own.

Most of the merchants are inspired by or associated with characters in Abomination Vaults, and a few come directly from that module. Each merchant has the shop name in its description, along with a brief bio or noteworthy information for each merchant.

I only created actors for the maps included in this module. Other possible merchants you can create for these maps are:

  • Tamily at the Otari Fisher with drinks and medieval junk food.

  • Oloria at Gallentine Deliveries, with stabling services.

  • Lardus at the Otari Garrison, with stabling services

I also included these merchant actors, but the actual scenes are part of Tianze's Gauntlight Extras:

  • The Rowdy Rockfish, with food, drinks, beds, baths, and stabling.

  • Dawnflower Library shop, with potions, clerical supplies, magical consumables and weapons, and runes.

I highly recommend the use of the Item Piles module to flesh out the merchants actors, and to add full buy/sell functionality, along with other tweaks such as store hours and dedicated inventory roll tables.

Characters from Abomination Vaults

In order to avoid a dependency upon the portraits and token art installed with Abomination Vaults, I recreated any actors that are needed for the various encounters.

Official Actors and Items

Everything in the Actors and Items tabs, except those I created as described above, come directly from the Compendium.

The maps are fully populated with the same actors in the Actors tab. The actors in the journals point to the compendium.

For convenience and playtesting purposes, I also included a set of Iconics, scaled to Level 2.

Recommended

I would like to take this opportunity to thank and recommend the creators of these additional modules and services.

Paid Modules

  • Abomination Vaults is not only an excellent adventure path, but it is a full multimedia experience with maps, actors, vignettes, music, ambient sounds, and scene-specific sounds. It is loaded with useful tools that you will find yourself using elsewhere. Plus, it is teaching me how to build better macros. :)

  • Troubles in Otari, is a series of short adventures from Paizo, which all take place in Otari and in the surrounding areas.

  • Mercenary Marketplace, which I used in Gauntlight Extras, and which helps you to build NPC actors based on character classes, jobs, or roles.

Free Modules

  • As a companion to this module, I cannot recommend Footsteps of Otari, by Mark Pearce enough. Mark's collection inspired me to create this one, and I only created maps that were not in his collection. It does include a number of redrawn maps from Abomination Vaults, but has no dependency on that module.

  • PF2e a shopping experience is a sweet little content module with one set of prebuilt shops for Otari merchants, and another set of leveled prebuilt shops suitable for any campaign.

  • Item Piles. I highly recommend the use of this module to bring more convenience and automation to the merchant actors. I liked this module so much that I almost included it as a dependency on this module. However, the specifics of how each merchant should operate should be up to the gamemaster.

Shop Rolltables.name: Shop Rolltables
Shop Rolltables.text:
If you use Item Piles, you will be able to use these rolltables to populate any loot actors that you have set as a "merchant" in the item pile setting for each loot actor.

Once you have set them up as merchant, go to the Populate tab, then add the rolltable.

Most of the rolltables do not have a weight of other than 1. Clodia's Clothery is the only exception, where I gave greater weight to the more common items.

An Invitation to the Osprey Club.name: An Invitation to the Osprey Club

Membership in the Osprey Club.name: Membership in the Osprey Club
Membership in the Osprey Club.text: At this point, the hero is a member of the Guild. What they do with this membership, and how the guild conducts its operation, is up to the individual gamemaster and player. The everyday running of the guild, and all its bylaws, is beyond the scope of this adventure.

Prescreening.name: Prescreening
Prescreening.text:
Before being offered a chance to join, members of the Osprey Club will conduct a number of clandestine checks to determine 1) if a suspected thief is actually a thief and 2) if they think the thief will be able to bring anything useful to the guild.They are alert for the following:

  1. Armor - is their armor quiet? If not, do they move quietly anyway?

  2. Weapons - do most of them have the finesse or agile traits?

  3. Movement - does the thief's dexterity appear to have at least a +2 bonus?

  4. Demeanor - does the thief seem overly selfish, greedy or treacherous?

    • Note: thieves are expected to have some of these qualities, but they will weed anyone who who seems so self-serving that they would not effectively work in a group.

  5. Once a prospective thief has passed all these tests, a member thief will attempt to engage them in conversation by asking innocuous questions about their goals in town and what they do for a living. While doing so, the member will attempt to pickpocket the prospective, going for either a consumable or a knife.Check: DC 20 Thievery to catch onto the theft. If caught, the thief will say "Very good," and hand the item back. Otherwise, the thief will say, "You dropped something," and hand the item back. The real test, however, is in how the prospective reacts to this obvious theft.

  6. If the prospective is outraged or indignant, or wanting to call a constable, the thief will offer a 5 gp bribe to forget about it. If they insist on calling the law, entry into the Osprey Club is closed for good.

  7. If violent, the thief will back off and offer a 5 gp bribe to forget about it. If they persist in violence, the other thieves will make their presence known, and the prospective will be thrown out and told never to return.

  8. If the prospective seems intrigued, or settles down after some initial outrage, then the thief will ask for a private conversation.

  9. In the private conversation, the prospective will be offered a chance to join "our little club" where they can get jobs and special discounts, but only if they can be loyal and agree to a series of challenges.If the prospective agrees, they will need to wait for Yinyasmira to break away in order to conduct Challenge 1.

Challenge 1 - Yinyasmira.name: Challenge 1 - Yinyasmira
Challenge 1 - Yinyasmira.text:
The first challenge is to talk to Yinyasmira. She conduct her interview while fishing at one of the open hatches, where the sound of the rushing waters below will mask the conversation.

She will ask if they understand why Yinyasmira selected this spot for their conversation.

She will ask probing questions about the prospective's Rogue's Racket, their purpose with their group, and the group's purpose in town.

There is no right or wrong answer to any of her questions. She is trying to determine if the prospective is likely to cause trouble for the group, and if the prospective is too evil or greedy to follow instructions and work well within a group.

Yinyasmira

CN female human smuggler 5
Perception DC 22, Will DC 20.
Skills: Avoid Notice, Balance, Conceal an Object, Create a Diversion - Trick, Create Forgery, Disable Device, Escape, Feint, Gather Information, Lie, Palm an Object, Sense Motive, Steal

@UUID[Actor.ui5mbNv2CuZxmkdO]{Yinyasmira}

Challenge Passing Standard

The prospective passed if Yinyasmira says they passed. And that is it. She has turned many skilled thieves away, including Carmen Rajani (who is nevertheless a frequent patron of the tavern).

The prospective can only progress onto challenge 2 or 3 if they pass this initial challenge.

Challenge 2 - Skills.name: Challenge 2 - Skills
Challenge 2 - Skills.text:
The challenges begin at midnight, after Crook's Nook closes and all the patrons have left.

This is a test of thievery, dexterity and stealth in a time crunch. This test should be conducted in Encounter mode.

  • First Round - Open the Lock

    • the prospective must open a poor lock on one of the hatches:

      • Two successful @Check[type:thievery|dc:15] checks to open (1 action each). The members will keep track of the number of attempts the prospective must make.

  • Next Two Rounds - Hide and Seek

    • At the beginning of this round, two members (Acrobats, see below) will bolt for opposite sides of the Underbridge, where they will attempt to find where the prospective hides in the steps below.

    • The thieves will arrive from opposite ends of the underbridge at the end of round 3.

    • the prospective must open the hatch (1 action) and jump down the hatch while swinging over to land on the boardwalk below (1 action).

      • One successful @Check[type:dexterity|dc:20] check

      • At least one successful @Check[type:hide|dc:20] checks before the thieves arrive.

  • Last Round, the prospective must remain hidden from the acrobats until found by both acrobats or until a time limit is called.

    • Three successful @Check[type:stealth|dc:20] checks against the DCs of each acrobat. They do not work together.

Opponents

2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.Tj03FbN4SSr0o953]{Acrobats}

Challenge Passing Standard

The minimum acceptable standards are:

  • In Step 1, the lock is opened in at least 3 actions.

  • In Step 2, the prospective makes it onto the boardwalk.

  • In Step 3, the prospective manages to stay hidden from at least one of the acrobats through at least one seek action.

Challenge 3 - Treachery Test.name: Challenge 3 - Treachery Test
Challenge 3 - Treachery Test.text:
The last challenge is thiefly combat. While in the area under the bridge, the prospective will be partnered with one member against two other members, while being observed by Yinyasmira and the rest of the club members.

The point of this exercise is not to see if the thief excels in combat, although judging combat skill is certainly part of it. The point of the thiefly combat challenge is to assess how well the prospective works with another as a team, how well they respond to frustration, and to assess their capacity for treachery.

As Guildmaster, Yinyasmera has had to put up with all manner of treachery, and she would rather not accept anyone that she judges as treacherous.

Therefore, the prospective will deliberately be set against someone who is more powerful than they are, and who will harass and frustrate the prospective as much as possible to see how they respond to frustration.

Ally

2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.Tj03FbN4SSr0o953]{Acrobats}

Opponents

2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.Tj03FbN4SSr0o953]{Acrobats}

1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.B09JfuBZHjcRXztU]{Burglar}

Challenge Passing Standard

Each of the members watching the battle will rate the prospective's overall performance on a simple 1 - 5 scale. A rating of 3 or greater by at least 5 out of 8 members is considered passing.

Conclusion.name: Conclusion
Conclusion.text:
The prospective has already passed Yinyasmira's challenge, so anyone who shows minimal competence and was not judged as treacherous is accepted into the guild on these terms:

Apprentice Member - the prospective fought honorably and passed Yinyasmira's challenge, but failed the other challenges. The prospective is paired up with a mentor and asked to improve their skills. They do not have access to the guildhall or the shop, and are forbidden to practice their skills within town without their mentor present.

Journeyman Member - the prospective fought honorably and passed at least one additional challenge. The prospective is paired up with a mentor and asked to improve their skills. They have access to the guildhall, but not the shop, and may practice their skills in town, on outsiders only, without their mentor present.

Member - the prospective fought honorably and passed all challenges. They have full access to the guildhall and shop. They may practice their skills in town, with extreme descretion. Outsiders are preferred targets.

Thirsty Alpaca Ruin.name: Thirsty Alpaca Ruin
Thirsty Alpaca Ruin.text:
Before you stands an impressive, rubble-filled pit. The townspeople have cleared away the larger sections of the walls and roof, and what remains is a jumble of building stones, lumber, bedding and furnishings.

A lean-to is set up near the north wall of the pit.

The pit is 6 to 8 feet deep, and climbing in and out is trivial with a rope, and only a DC 10 without one.

Strange Lights

If the players visit after full dark, two light near the southern end of the ruin will activate. The dragon mage plants these lights for a few hours nightly in order to keep the investigations of the curious and brave away from their lean-to.

Spooky Sounds

Day or night, when the players draw near the lean-to, the kobolds within will begin to make spooky moaning sounds, in order to drive away the timid.

The Dead Kobold

Near the center of the pit, a bloodstain and bloody footprints leads to the body of a kobold warrior.

Use this macro to make the kobold visible:

@UUID[Macro.ZxEchksOJCeaGiLk]{Toggle Dead Kobold Visibility}

Note: the kobold is represented by a tile rather than an actor, to avoid situations where a mod or the system forces dead token invisibility.

The kobold has already been stripped of all valuables.

The Lean-To

Behind the lean-to, two kobold warriors and one kobold scout are hiding and keeping watch on the PCs. If they get too close, they will start their attack with distance attacks. One warrior will attempt to go down into the hole to warn their leader.

1: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary.Actor.rPaHIh0ICnTLnRO6]{Kobold Scout}

2: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary.Actor.r9w1n85mp9Ip4QiS]{Kobold Warrior}

Kobold Warren Entry.name: Kobold Warren Entry
Kobold Warren Entry.text:
The ladder descends to an area that is mostly to the north of the area where the Thirsty Alpaca once stood. When it collapsed, it entirely collapsed one tunnel, plus a whole network of rooms. Another tunnel was partially collapsed. The kobolds are working to clear out the collapsed areas.

As you descend the ladder, you see a dim light reflecting on a rocky floor below. Once at the bottom, you find yourself in a cavern that has been partially collapsed in the destruction of the inn above.

Piles of rubble and earth surround you.

A flickering light is to the north.

A blocked tunnel is to the south.

Kobold Warren.name: Kobold Warren
Kobold Warren.text:
Beyond the piles of rubble, three kobolds are seated at a dilapidated table, dining on disgusting food and speaking together in their muttery language. A campfire burns near the table.

(Image courtesy of Bing Image Creator)

One Red Kobold Dragon Mage leads this intrepid crew of kobold invaders:

1: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary.Actor.CJuHwIRCAgTB1SEl]{Red Kobold Dragon Mage}

1: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary.Actor.rPaHIh0ICnTLnRO6]{Kobold Scout}

1: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.troubles-in-otari-bestiary.Actor.fhItdltCmcAZkvcI]{Kobold Trapmaster}

2:@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary.Actor.r9w1n85mp9Ip4QiS]{Kobold Warrior}

The Kobold Scout is asleep in the northwest warren, and one of the kobold warriors is asleep in the southwest warren.

Encounter Notes

  • If the kobold warrior from the surface manages to get down the ladder to warn the leader, and if the heroes immediately pursue them down, then add one kobold warrior to the battle, along with the two kobolds from the caverns near the entry. Awaken the kobolds in the sleeping caverns.

  • If the PCs engage all of these kobolds at once, it would make the battle very tough. However, the kobolds will not pursue the PCs back up the ladder. Plus, they will only be on the alert for an hour or two before they will disperse to their usual activities.

  • The Red Kobold Dragon Mage has an Onyx Dog. To avoid overbalancing this encounter, the Dragon Mage should fumble when attempting to activate the dog, and it falls to the ground. @Check[perception|dc:15] to see the dog fall. Otherwise, it should be easy to spot the dog while searching for loot.

  • The Kobold Scout and Kobold Warriors in that are asleep in the warrens will take one complete round to wake up, get up, grab a weapon, and start moving toward the battle.

Kobold Tactics

  • All kobolds have a sneak attack, which inflicts extra damage. While they do not roll their initiative with stealth, they can use an action to hide and thus make their opponent Off-Guard to them.

  • Kobold Warriors have the Hurried Retreat perk, which allows them to dart away with limited opportunity for Reactive Strikes.

  • The Kobold Trapmaster can deploy a trap with their Quick Trap action, which sets up a spike trap in three actions. The Trapmaster should only attempt this while in a concealed condition, or while retreating.

  • The Kobold Scout has a crossbow, and is tougher than the warriors.

Treasure

Each kobold carried most of his or her valuables on their person. Additionally, each has possessions in sacks near or under their sleeping mats. All of these items are collected in the @UUID[Actor.eNli7XDXWRou3i0C]{Kobold Warren Treasure} token near the firepit.

Experience

This entire adventure should be worth about 100 experience points for each player.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
This is a short adventure designed for heroes who have begun to establish a name for themselves in Otari, perhaps by finishing the Beginner Box adventure, but have not delved too deeply into any other Otari-based adventure.

How it Starts

The adventure begins when Magiloy, the proprietress of the Crow's Casks Tavern, sends a messenger asking the party to come see her.

(Note: this is an adventure hook from Abomination Vaults.)

Magiloy is a former pirate - ahem - seafarer - and is also an accomplished alchemist. She runs the most popular inn in town. She is concerned with not only the collapse of the inn, but also with some more recent developments.

When they arrive, she takes them out the back door and gestures across the river.

That crater across the river from here—something needs to be done about it. The people who live near it are saying that strange lights and spooky sounds have started coming from it. Plus, something constructed a lean-to within it. I'm worried that whatever is undermining that place might cause some sort of collapse near the river itself, which could wash out this entire area.

Some potential questions and answers:

What happened to the owner?

It was terrible. We pulled his body out of the rubble, along with several members of his family. We had to assume that the rest are buried deeper in the rubble.

Why haven't the guards dealt with this?

Well, they were guarding the place, but the goings on over there—especially at night—have them a bit spooked. There're here to guard the town against brigands and pirates, and they do well enough against that sort. But they want no part of investigating spooks.

When did the lean-to show up?

Two nights ago. The guards went to pull it down, but the lights and sounds scared them away. They're trying to decide what to do, but I'm tired of the dithering, and so are my neighbors.

After they have finished their questions, she will add:

As a reward, I can give you each 10 gold, plus I'll put in a petition with the mayor that you be granted the deed to the land. I could also get some of the neighbors to sign the petition. I can't guarantee anything, but with what you've already done since you came here, I think the old man will want to keep you around.

Further Investigations

If the players ask the neighbors of the Thirsty Alpaca about what happened, they will confirm the weird sights and sounds, but have little else to offer. They now avoid the area as best they can, and are keen to have the problem solved.

Afterward.name: Afterward
Afterward.text:
Once the heroes report success to Magiloy, she is delighted and offers the 10 gold that she promised for each party member.

She also circulates the petition, as she promised, among the neighbors on both sides of the river, and delivers the petition to the mayor, herself.

The problem of the tunnel beyond the collapse still needs to be solved, and its existence helps the Mayor to decide to simply give the PCs the property.

Therefore, three days later, Magiloy is able to present the deed to the property, herself.

Hazard.name: Hazard
Hazard.text:
Just to the west of the ladder is a hazard:

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.abomination-vaults-bestiary.Actor.6NijRSpkIuQpSxUp]{Spike Launcher}

@Check[perception|dc:19] to detect the spike launcher.

Blocked Passages.name: Blocked Passages
Blocked Passages.text:
To the south are two partially-excavated areas where the Thirsty Alpaca actually caved in. Within each passage, a kobold is working clear the rubble. They are focused on their work and will not have a chance of noticing the PCs until they come within 15 feet.

2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary.Actor.r9w1n85mp9Ip4QiS]{Kobold Warrior}

Glimpse of Passage Beyond.name: Glimpse of Passage Beyond
Glimpse of Passage Beyond.text:
If the players search the rear of the southeast tunnel, they can find places that provide visibility to the tunnel beyond, showing that the tunnel continues in a southeasterly direction after the blocked point.

The destination of the passage is beyond the scope of this adventure, but it could easily lead to a larger kobold warren, to one of the other dungeons around Otari, the basement of someone in league with the kobolds, or somewhere else, entirely.

Home Invasion.name: Home Invasion
Home Invasion.text:
Background

In this encounter, a family of boggards invades the heroes' home.

This adventure should occur not long after the heroes have moved in, after they return to their house after a few days away.

This should be a tough challenge for Level 2 characters. If your characters are a different level, either add or remove opponents to adjust the encounter level.

Creatures

For this encounter, I have tweaked the Boggards into a variant that lives along the seashore.

The only functional change is that I changed their Swamp Passage into Sandy Passage, so they ignore difficult terrain while in sandy environments. It should not apply to this encounter, though.

@UUID[Actor.JlgB5nKgzgnGLYBI]{Sea Boggard Scout}

@UUID[Actor.SCotNnN2jNvGk1AJ]{Sea Boggard Warrior}

@UUID[Actor.uUYG3eEjC69CPyLr]{Boggard Shoreseer}

Setup

Most of the boggards aren't interested in the upper house, but after an initial ransacking, have taken over the stable, and the area underneath. The only exception is the Shoreseer, who has moved into the central room with his bodyguard.

When they arrive, any fires have been put out, and every interior door is open.

Stable

This is a guard post. If any intruders approach, the guards will make noise to either frighten away the cowardly, or lure in the brave.

2 Sea Boggard Scouts

1 Sea Boggard Warrior

XP: 120

Under the Porch

These boggards are in the area between the house and the workshop buildings, where they have set up a nest.

4 Sea Boggard Scouts under the porch.

XP: 120

Interior

The Shoreseer has taken over the central room with his bodyguard, but will set up an ambush in the central hallways if he becomes aware of an attack.

Turn off all lights

Open all interior doors

Place creatures:

1 Boggard Shoreseer

1 Sea Boggard Scout

XP: 120

Progress of Encounter

  1. When the heroes arrive home, they hear a door slam in the direction of the stable, which should alert them that something is amiss in that direction.

  2. When they approach the stable, the door slams open and the encounter begins.

  3. When two of the boggards have fallen, the last one should attempt to to get away by running to the south and alerting the boggards under the front porch.

  4. Ideally, the four boggards under the porch should then join the battle, which would make it one extended encounter.

  5. When most have fallen, one of the Scouts tries to get away to alert the Shoreseer. If that happens, the scout and the warrior should attempt to flank the first person who enters the central hallway.

  6. If the heroes withdraw from the map for an extended recovery, then the Shoreseer and his trusty lieutenant will also withdraw after assessing his losses, and they will not attempt to take the house again. He will bring his treasure with him, but might leave behind a couple of things in the rush of his departure.

Treasure

Each boggard is wearing leather armor that is somewhat uncommon and therefore is worth more than similar, more common leathers. Or it will be if the heroes clean it up before attempting to sell them. Additionally, the Shoreseer kept all their accumulated treasure in the central room:

@UUID[Actor.l7OEHrqvnxSmUkGj]{Boggard Treasure}

Playtest Notes

  1. I playtested this as one extended encounter using the Leveled Iconics, who approached from the cliff path. The battle wiped out all of Ezren's 1st level spells and at one point, Kyra had to keep casting healing spells at Val to keep him alive while he was flanked and his Warrior opponent was benefiting from the Runic Weapon spell.

  2. Ideally, the heroes should take any opportunity for a rest and recovery period before taking on the Shoreseer in the central room of the house. Maybe they could even hide nearby and ambush him when he tries to get away.

  3. The area just inside the central hallway makes a wonderful kill zone for the defenders. This is where Val was flanked. Probably not the wisest decision, but he figured he was tough enough to withstand a couple of frogs.

Encounter - Rival Gang.name: Encounter - Rival Gang
Encounter - Rival Gang.text:
This encounter should take place late in the morning, once all the vendors have set up for the day, and the lunch rush is beginning.

Start the encounter when at least one of the heroes draws near Keeleno's stall.

A group of thieves, wearing clothing and items intended to deceive everyone into thinking they are from the Osprey Club, attack the market from the grassy area to the east of Keeleno's stall.

After the attack begins, Keeleno will snarl to the nearest hero:

I hear you and your friends have been helping folks out around town. Help me rout these thugs and I'll pay you well.

Background

The Osprey Club is the local thieves guild. It is run by Yinyasmira at the Crook's Nook, and she is careful to ensure the members never "hit" any of the town's businesses. This keeps her on neutral terms with the Mayor.

The thieves are from a gang to the southeast. They decided to hit the town with the intention of making Yinyasmira look bad, and to sour the relationship between the Osprey Club and the people and merchants of Otari.

It is a clumsy attack, but still is a danger to the vendors and customers.

Bandit Gang

2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.KPUDfkVpemug2gKj]{Bandit } - He attackes with a hatchet or sling, and is able to demoralize his opponent as a free action. Such opponents are Off-Guard to him.

4 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pfs-season-1-bestiary.Actor.ZMGXiRuVZ8r7hQVe]{Bandit Scout} - They keep their distance with shortbows or Alchemists Fire. Three have been weakened; adjust as necessary.

Tactics

The gang will move swiftly to demoralize the vendors and customers, steal as much as they can grab, and cause mayhem. Then they will retreat to a boat that is waiting at the docks. They will try to take out Keeleno early, as they consider him to be the greatest threat.

Their plan involves avoiding any guards as much as possible, and especially avoiding getting in range of their Attacks of Opportunity. They watch carefully so as to attack when the guards' attention is elsewhere.

They did not count on a capable group of adventurers at the market.

If you care to create an additional map, this encounter could easily turn into a thrilling chase down the road to the Fishery and the docks, and maybe even onto the boat itself.

Allies

Three guards are on hand to assist, but will mostly be concerned with protecting bystanders:

3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.rsATu823vatRe7QJ]{Guard} - The Guard and Guard Archer share the same actor type. They also have an Attack of Opportunity. They have crossbows and bludgeoning weapons, including a sap.

The vendors are all non-combatants with the possible exception of the following:

Keeleno, Level 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.cAOWcPIjtZYXYZ3i]{Merchant}

Zeek, Level 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.8WFGygPv7UHh7zdJ]{Apothecary}

Bethela, Level 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.sKSfQmJMEsj8QN12]{Adept}

If you decide to add these to the combat, pull the NPC actors in from the compendium, and scale them accordingly. For added color, you might want to have them grab items from their vendor tables to assist in combat.

If you do add them to the combat, don't forget to add additional enemy combatants, or the encounter will quickly become trivial.

Experience

This encounter is worth 40 experience points.

Treasure

Keeleno makes good on his promise, and he pays the heroes five gold pieces each.

In addition to the loot on the enemy tokens, they have a few valuables, which the guard captain gives to the heroes:

@UUID[Actor.g80tntJEkpVGYXFC]{Bandit Loot}

And finally, when Yinyasmira hears of the plot against her, and if the bandits were killed or captured, she will also pay 5 gold pieces each.

This could possibly spawn another quest in which Yinyasmira or the Mayor sends the heroes down the coast to investigate the bandit gang.

An Accusation.name: An Accusation
An Accusation.text:
Note: This encounter assumes that the heroes have already become to amass a bit of a reputation for themselves as problem solvers.

Setup

Bring some other townspeople into the tavern, and seat them throuought the inn. Activate Zeek near the oven.

Starting the Encounter

As the group relaxes one evening at Crow's Casks, fighting words erupt at a card table: "You're cheating!"

The two card players at a table along the western wall jump to their feet, and fists begin to fly. Two others at the nearby bar s rush over to join in. The rest of the patrons jump up to watch.

Magiloy rushes over to the heroes.

I'll pay you five gold each if you can put a stop to this brawl without killing anyone. Oh, and a bonus if nothing is damaged!

The Brawlers

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pfs-season-1-bestiary.Actor.XiGTud90i1WkJYz2]{Offended Gambler} - He is pretty sure he was cheated, and will not give up easily.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.npc-gallery.Actor.DFurZlcpcNrUmmER]{Ruffian} - The ruffian did the cheating, and he is the toughest of the group. Once the fight starts, he doesn't want stop for fear of going to jail, but also will not fight to the death.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.fall-of-plaguestone-bestiary.Actor.BgBTntoz1qQ3h1X5]{Drunken Farmer} - The farmer just took advantage of the chaos to blow off steam, and is easily subdued. He takes the side of the ruffian.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.extinction-curse-bestiary.Actor.s6Yfy1AgPp4ky7QI]{Drunken Brawler} - This guy likes any excuse for a fight, and he has plenty of liquid bravery running through his veins. He takes the side of the gambler.

The Brawl

After the fight begins, the patrons of the inn will clear a space around the four combatants. The fight should be chaotic, but none of the participants are out for blood.

Every once in a while, Magiloy will yell that if they stop now, she won't summon the constables. She'll give them 3 opportunities to stop, once each round.

Options for Nonviolent Resolution

Here are some ways that the heroes might use to resolve the situation without undue violence:

  • Talk some sense into them with @Check[diplomacy|dc:15]

  • Disarm combatants: @Check[disarm|dc:15]

  • Separate combatants: @Check[athletics|dc:15]

  • Distract with a diversion via deception @Check[deception|dc:15]

  • Demoralize: @Check[intimidation|dc:15]

The possibilities are limitless.

Aftermath

Once the combatants are subdued, Magiloy will extract a certain price from each of them in return for not summoning the constable.

They all must also help clean up the mess while the heroes stand guard.

  • From the gambler, she demands his set of ivory dice. If he objects, she will say that he should have come to her, rather than starting a fight.

  • From the ruffian, she demands he forfeit his dubious winnings - 12 gold pieces.

  • From the farmer, she wants two sacks of grain.

  • From the brawler, she wants a week's worth of labor.

Experience

Assuming a 2nd level party:

40 XP for subduing the ruffians

20 XP bonus if no NPCs are killed.

Treasure

Magiloy will provide the gold that promised, plus will split the 12 gold pieces with the offended gambler and the heroes. She will give the ivory dice to the heroes, and will throw in five potions.

Amounts assume 4 players.

@UUID[Actor.iZm7lK2pnQm9pn2h]{Rowdy Patron Loot}

Crow's Casks.name: Crow's Casks
Crow's Casks.text:
Crow's Casks is part brewery, one part alchemy shop, and one part tavern. Magiloy is one busy bird.

This tavern features an alchemy shop in the NE corner, a shrine to Cayden Cailean in the SW corner, a fireplace with a place for a bard or storyteller in the east wall, and a bar just inside the entry.

A few notes:

  • Magiloy brews and serves her own mead, ale and beer. Her still is in the back. She also has whiskey available.

  • The menu features a selection of breads, cheeses, meats and fish, but never poultry or egg products.

  • The windows are made of oilcloth, which is a sturdy medieval window covering that is translucent, but is otherwise opaque. This is why there are no windows on the wall layer.

    • However, there are individual walls in front of each window, to allow you to quickly change the window type in case a rowdy patron tears through the oilcloth.

    • Also, a light in front of each window will illuminate during daylight hours, casting an indirect light.

  • Merchant Actor: @UUID[Actor.vAR07Am0iB8uhlE1]{Crow's Casks}

  • Merchant Actor: @UUID[Actor.mGmjwfNEVx95hNS8]{Zeek} (in the kitchen with visibility off. Should only be visible when the market is closed.)

  • The actors from the @UUID[JournalEntry.sdhbLcAPYiE7Lkcm]{Rowdy Gamblers} encounter are also on the scene.

Bar

Mags likes to hang out near the bar. She keeps six varieties of ale, mead and beer on tap.

Kitchen

Mags manages to keep something cooking most of the time, rotating food on and off the fire, and preparing it on a large table. Her apprentice, Zeek, works here when not running the market stall. She also has some part-time barmaids and barkeeps that you can populate as desired.

Alchemy Workstation

This workstation is in the NE corner. If the heroes earn her support, she will take a fledgling alchemist on as a part time assistant. Most of the time, such assistants will be manning the bar or the ovens. However, she will lend her assistance in alchemical crafting, providing a +1 bonus for her superior equipment, and a +1 bonus for her superior skill.

Alchemy Items for Sale

This area is south of the alchemy workstation, and has a variety of potions for sale. Powders and other items are on the lower shelves.

Tavern

The bar separates the kitchen and alchemy shop from the tavern to the south. The tables in this are are widely-spaced apart, giving each table an unusual amount of privacy.

The tables on the west side of the tavern are often taken over by card players.

Bread Board

In the south end of the tavern is the bread board. Freshly cooked items are placed here, and are included with the cost of a full meal.

Shrine

In the SW corner is a shrine to Cayden Caelean. It features an oversized, two-handled pewter stein.

Magiloy fills it each morning as an offering, and she will give away the contents throughout the day whenever she thinks someone deserves it.

The stein can fill four ordinary tankards.

Fireplace

In front of the cheerful hearth is a chair for any bard or storyteller to have a seat and spin some yarns.

Crook's Nook and Bridge.name: Crook's Nook and Bridge
Crook's Nook and Bridge.text:
Crook's Nook was originally a fishery built on the bridge. When Yinyasmira inherited it, she first converted it to a tavern with its audacious name, and gradually established the Osprey Club.

The bridge is now affectionately known as Crook's Bridge.

The structure has four levels:

  • The Underbridge

  • The Tavern level

  • The Upper level

  • Yinyasmira's Private Apartments (outside of the scope of this module … for now)

From here, you can launch one of the heroes on the path to becoming a member of the Osprey Club: @UUID[JournalEntry.81Vsse742fCE9COq]{An Invitation to the Osprey Club}.

The Underbridge.name: The Underbridge
The Underbridge.text:
One can access the Underbridge by walking down the slopes on either side of the bridge.

Gravel Paths

Gravel paths on each side of the river can be used as possible fishing spots. Well within the shady spots are convenient stone benches.

The water here is not deep, but at this point, as it rushes the last distance toward the ocean, the current gets quite rapid.

If one of the heroes ends up in the water, they need to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swim} (@Check[type:athletics|dc:13]{Athletics}) to avoid being swept out into the bay.

If they fail a check, they will need two additional checks at the same difficulty level to fight the current enough to swim back to shore.

The Walkway

This broad boardwalk has rope bridges equipped with convenient ties for fishing rods. There is also a crane used for raising and lowering nets. Yinyasmira lowers and raises the net several times a day, catching a wide variety of fish from the brackish coastal water.

To successfully fish from the bridge, the hero needs a survival check: @Check[type:survival|dc:15].

The Tavern Level.name: The Tavern Level
The Tavern Level.text:
This cozy tavern level has fishing hatches, twin bars and fireplaces, and a lovely view of the river beyond.

Stairways Leading Up

At the southwest and southeast corners of the building, wooden stairs lead up.

Twin Bars

Identical bars are at the west and east sides of the building, and each seats six. Under each bar are kegs with ale, beer and mead.

Tables for Four

Cozy tables for four are each places a discreet distance away from each other, allowing for mostly private conversations.

Riverview Windows

These wired windows allow for a lovely view of the river to the north.

Fishing Hatches

Three fishing hatches allow access to the river below with one of the fishing rods between the two fireplaces. Toggle their visibility as needed with these macros:

@UUID[Macro.C4awKLQDBhDo8Nlu]{Toggle Left Hatch Visibility}

@UUID[Macro.HdNOTXq3iNBE2qdh]{Toggle Middle Hatch Visibility}

@UUID[Macro.1wl30MTr9uczQGqV]{Toggle Right Hatch Visibility}

To successfully fish from the hatch, the hero needs a survival check: @Check[type:survival|dc:15].

It could also provide a way for a quick getaway, as a nimble thief could either swing out to the south into the river below, or swing out to the north onto the boardwalk.

Check: @Check[type:acrobatics|dc:18|name:Swing onto Boardwalk] to swing onto the boardwalk.

NOTE: the town constabulary is wise to this method of escape, and if they send anyone to Crook's Nook to detain a suspected criminal, they always have guards ready under the bridge to give chase.

Twin Fireplaces

These are both lit to ensure efficient kitchen operations in all but the hottest months.

Kitchen Area

This well-stocked and efficient kitchen serves both full meals and medieval junk food.

The Upper Level.name: The Upper Level
The Upper Level.text:
Twin Staircases

These staircases are at the SW and SE corners of the building.

Single Bedrooms

Each room has two single beds and a small sturdy chest with a good lock. A side table is between the beds, and a sconce is on the wall beside the door.

Double Bedrooms

Each room has a double bed, a large sturdy chest with a good lock, two side tables, and a sconce on the wall beside the door.

Flop Room

This common sleeping room has 10 bedframes, each with a straw mattress. They are reasonably clean, but not entirely. The two fireplaces sometimes keeps the room too warm, but two large windows opposite the fireplace can help. A table between the fireplaces seats six.

Check: @Check[type:fortitude|dc:12|]to avoid being @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} by bedbugs.

Osprey Club Headquarters

Getting In

The Osprey Club Headquarters have magical good-quality locks on the doors, which requires 5 consecutive checks to get in:

5 consecutive @Check[type thievery|dc:30] checks.

Upon any failure, a bell rings within, and the locks reset.

There is a hidden panel at face-level. Any ringing of the bell will be investigated.

Room Interior

This room has the following features:

  • Ample seating in front of the two fireplaces.

  • Two tables with comfortable chairs.

  • The guildmaster's desk

  • Two sturdy cabinets for the Osprey Club Store.

The room is almost always occupied by at least a thief or two.

Osprey Club Store

Either Yinyasmira or a trusted lieutenant mans the store. Whoever is in charge of the store is in charge of the room.

The desk and each cabinet has Good quality locks, which require 5 @Check[type thievery|dc:30] checks to open.

@UUID[Actor.uOZVSXUt2ZSw8Dsq]{Osprey Club Store}

Note: In this room, Yinyasmira is represented by a regular NPC actor, rather than the merchant actor with the same name, which is her guise on the first floor.

@UUID[Actor.ui5mbNv2CuZxmkdO]{Yinyasmira}

Stairs Up

The stairs lead up to Yinyasmira's private quarters, which are beyond the scope of this module (for now).

Fish Camp Base.name: Fish Camp Base
Fish Camp Base.text:
This map is based on the Fish Camp that originally appeared in Troubles in Otari. It is rotated 90 degrees from the original map. I am including it here as a potential home base for your heroes.

Location

In the original scenario, the Fish Camp was some distance from town - certainly not within the town limits. From my own experience, your heroes might prefer a more convenient location.

Therefore, in my own game, I moved it to the far side of the logging flume, on a wide portion of the cliff (not represented on the Otari map), twenty to thirty feet above the beach. A switchback path leads down to the beach.

From here, town is just a short walk down the beach and under the flume.

Why Are All the Windows Doors?

As you probably guessed from the other scenes in this module, I am a big believer in period-specific construction, and glass simply would not be feasible for most buildings. Magiloy's place has oilcloth window coverings, but shutters are more appropriate for a fish camp, which is probably subject to some harsh weather.

Therefore, all windows are actually small doors, to represent shutters that the players should be able to open and close. A small character could easily use these to enter and exit.

Encounter

I have prepared an encounter for this scene: @UUID[JournalEntry.mW1pwcr2Wi5l31gp.JournalEntryPage.yhHq5Eif2VdeuPfi]{Home Invasion}

A Tour

The house includes:

  • Four single bedrooms

  • One double room in the center of the house. This could be for humanoids with darkvision.

  • Kitchen with stove and oven

  • Dining Room

  • Living Room

  • Entry

  • Study

Outer buildings, with

  • Alchemy Crafting Station

  • General Crafting Station

  • Magical Crafting Station with separate rune crafting and scroll writing areas.

  • Wraparound Porch

  • Two Storage Sheds

  • 1-Horse Stable with Storage

Home Base Decorating.name: Home Base Decorating
Home Base Decorating.text:
I left some room for a bit of creativity and personalization for the players. I think it is worth part of a game session for a bit of home base decorating, especially since a great deal of downtime will be spent here.

Ideally, each bedroom should get either a bedroll or a mattress on the bed, and each should have a functional chest using a loot actor.

You can download asses for free at Forgotten Adventures.

Bedroom Furnishings

  • Bedrolls - https://forgottenadventures.piwigo.com/index?/category/811-bedrolls_and_sleeping_bags

  • Mattresses with blankets - https://forgottenadventures.piwigo.com/index?/category/987-single_beds

  • Chests - https://forgottenadventures.piwigo.com/index?/category/934-chests

Outdoor Fun

Additionally, a campfire is always fun. Pick a spot and put down either a campfire or a more elaborate outdoor cooking area:

  • Campfires - https://forgottenadventures.piwigo.com/index?/category/1047-campfires_and_firepits

  • Outdoor Cooking - https://forgottenadventures.piwigo.com/index?/category/2004-outdoor_cooking

For the fire, I put a flickering fire on the stove in the kitchen. You could copy that light for the fire itself, and then make another copy using the "flickering" special effect option, and extend the range to 40/20.

Trees and Shrubs

You can find trees and plants here:

  • Flora: https://forgottenadventures.piwigo.com/index?/category/952-trees

I like to use the "Tree Tops" as overhead tiles set on Fade with 50% occlusion. If you really want to get fancy, download the matching shadow and put it under the tree.

The Decorating Session

A decorating session that involves the players will involve a little setup, but should be fun. I could not find any way to give players the ability to drop tiles onto the map, so here's what I came up with.

  • Download a selection of the tiles linked above and put it in a "tiles" folder of your game world. Don't put it in the Tianze's Otari Extras folder, because then it would be overwritten on the next update.

  • Then, put a copy of the same folders into a cloud drive such as Dropbox, OneDrive or Google Drive, and share it with your players so they can browse it.

  • Next, have each player claim a bedroom, and walk through each player one by one, choosing bed and chest options.

  • As they pick things out, pull the tiles out of the tiles folder and position as desired.

Try not to let your players go too wild, or you will bog down your scene with too many assets.

Dawnflower Library Store.text:
The Library sells items and weapons, but will only purchase items that would fit in with their usual stock.

They absolutely will not purchase any item that they perceive as evil. They will urge the heroes to leave any such items with them for disposal.

They will cast spells, such as for disease curing and curse removals, for the same cost it would be to make a scroll for the same spell.

If, as part of a curse removal, a hero needs to be rid of a cursed item, they accept such items for disposal free of charge, but may ask for a quest to facilitate any difficult-to-destroy items.

She carries clothing in a variety of sizes for small and medium creatures, and can make alternations to fit.

Clodia is a true artist, even if she has humble means. She loves nothing more to see someone beautifully clothed in her work.

She opens her shop at noon, so she can take advantage of the morning light for her work.

Bethela is seventeen years old, and recently returned from magical studies in Absalom.

Even though her family lives in town, she is accustomed to her independence and now rents a room from Alymora Inkleholtz.

In the mornings, she sells magical items from Wrin's Wonders and Odd Stories, and in the afternoons she tutors the Inlkeholtz children.

Larger societies rely on those with the authority and the ability to interpret and enforce laws. In good-aligned societies, these officials carry out their duties fairly.
